verdicts.name: Sema MCP Bridge (kill the slash commands)
verdicts.notes: Every named API exists with the claimed capability. Mid-session registerTool is real and auto-activating: loader.js:175-180 does Map.set + runtime.refreshTools(); agent-session.js:1782 binds that to _refreshToolRegistry(), which (agent-session.js:1902-1908) adds any tool name not in previousRegistryNames to the active set and calls setActiveToolsByName (agent-session.js:550-564), which rebuilds the system prompt (`this._baseSystemPrompt = this._rebuildSystemPrompt(...)`). Correct that no unregisterTool exists — setActiveTools is at types.d.ts:893, registerFlag at 857. Sema side confirmed: server.rs handle_request dispatches exactly initialize/ping/tools/list/tools/call, protocol 2024-11-05, listChanged:false at server.rs:169; Sandbox::allow_all() at main.rs:921 in the mcp arm; --include/--exclude filtering via is_tool_allowed (tools.rs:760-777; cited 764-779, minor drift). Line-delimited JSON-RPC confirmed (server writes one JSON line + \n, silent on notifications). Only nits: tools/list recompute is via global_env.iter_bindings at tools.rs:726 (not 558), and the long-lived child must be spawned with node:child_process (pi.exec runs to completion — unsuitable for a persistent server).

verdicts.name: /forge — Create-a-Tool flow (Claude Code /agents, but for deftools)
verdicts.notes: All mechanisms check out. ctx.ui.input (types.d.ts:73), pi.sendMessage with customType + triggerTurn (types.d.ts:867-870), registerTool for forge_submit fine. The load-bearing claim that sema's --timeout is a parsed no-op is CONFIRMED: main.rs:977 destructures `timeout: _timeout` and run_eval (main.rs:1625) never receives it — pi.exec's timeout (exec.d.ts ExecOptions) is indeed mandatory. JSON envelope fields ok/error_msg/error_hint/error_line/error_col confirmed at main.rs:1646-1670; `tool?` predicate exists (sema-llm/builtins.rs:4177); SEMA_HOME resolution confirmed (sema-core home.rs:4-13, resolution $SEMA_HOME > $HOME/.sema); tools/list recomputed from live env every call confirmed (tools.rs:726). registerTool from inside another tool's execute is legal — only guard is runtime.assertActive (loader.js:175). pi.appendEntry at types.d.ts:879. --sandbox strict and --no-llm flags exist on Commands::Eval (main.rs:972-980).

verdicts.name: Live Workflow Widget (journal-tailing sema_workflow_run tool)
verdicts.notes: Pi surface fully supported: execute() receives onUpdate (types.d.ts:361) which drives tool_execution_update and partial renderResult (ToolRenderResultOptions.isPartial, types.d.ts:303; ToolRenderContext.state, types.d.ts:316); ctx.ui.setWidget accepts a component factory (types.d.ts:97-99); execute's `signal` param gives Esc-cancellation (note: Esc aborts the whole turn, not just this tool). Sema side confirmed: SEMA_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID seam (sema-workflow context.rs:33,626); journal writes one JSON line + immediate flush, crash leaves valid prefix (journal.rs write()); events.resume-N.jsonl segments confirmed (journal.rs:19,195-201); full event vocabulary confirmed in event.rs — run.started with phases[] (event.rs:46-51), phase.started, agent.started/agent.result/agent.tool_call, budget (per-event, summable), run.ended, auth.required; exit code 2 for needs-auth confirmed (main.rs ~1363-1367 with format_needs_auth_guidance). One risk-note correction: run.started.code_version is NOT empty when run via `sema workflow run` — main.rs:1337-1342 unconditionally sets SEMA_WORKFLOW_CODE_VERSION to a content hash before eval; it's only empty/skipped when the env seam is unset (e.g. embedded runs). metadata.json fallback is still fine but unnecessary for CLI-launched runs.

verdicts.name: Workflow Runs Overlay Dashboard
verdicts.notes: ctx.ui.custom with {overlay, overlayOptions, onHandle} confirmed at types.d.ts:116-126; OverlayOptions supports anchor "top-right", width "60%" (SizeValue = number | `${n}%`), maxHeight — pi-tui tui.d.ts:59-104; OverlayHandle.setHidden(boolean) confirmed (tui.d.ts:116). registerShortcut(KeyId) at types.d.ts:852 and its handler receives ExtensionContext which includes ui.custom. docs/tui.md Overlays section exists (starting ~line 109) including dispose-on-close semantics. ctx.ui.setStatus confirmed (types.d.ts:79); ctx.mode guard (types.d.ts:211) — correct that ui.custom is TUI-only. GET /api/runs mtime-scan precedent confirmed at workflow_view.rs:232 (cited 301 — minor drift). Skipping index.db for direct JSONL parsing is sound; events cap sizes as claimed.

verdicts.name: create_sema_tool — the self-extending loop
verdicts.notes: The core loop is real end-to-end. registerTool callable from inside another tool's execute: loader.js:175-180 only calls runtime.assertActive, then Map.set + refreshTools → _refreshToolRegistry auto-adds the new name to active tools (agent-session.js:1902-1908) and rebuilds the system prompt via setActiveToolsByName (550-564), and agent.state.tools is swapped live — available next turn. ui.confirm available on execute's ctx (types.d.ts:71). deftool is a VM special form (special_forms.rs:58) binding into the shared global env; tools/list recomputed from iter_bindings every call (tools.rs:726). Collision claims verified EXACTLY: across-extension first-registration-wins (runner.js getAllRegisteredTools uses `if (!toolsByName.has(name))`, runner.js:252-262); within-extension last-wins (Map.set overwrite). One addition: in _refreshToolRegistry extension tools DO override built-in tools of the same name (definitionRegistry.set runs after builtins), so the prefix-generated-tools mitigation also protects builtins, not just other extensions. --timeout no-op claim re-confirmed (main.rs:977).

verdicts.name: Tool Library with lazy proxy (progressive disclosure)
verdicts.notes: Mechanism is supported but one detail in the spawn line is wrong as written: `sema mcp ~/.sema/pi-tools/*.sema` relies on shell glob/tilde expansion — sema does not glob and a child spawned with array args (no shell) won't expand `~` or `*`; the extension must expand the glob itself (fs.readdir/globSync) and pass explicit absolute file paths. Everything else checks out: filepath mode confirmed (main.rs:926-936 `for file in files { read_source_file → eval }` after llm/auto-configure); hiding via `_`-prefix and `:mcp/expose #f` confirmed (tools.rs:730-736, plus mcp/-namespaced meta stripping at tools.rs:32,415); json_args_to_sema named→positional coercion confirmed (tools.rs ~322); registerTool for hot-tool promotion fine; `sema pkg publish` exists (pkg.rs:1671 cmd_publish). The single-proxy-tool design has no Pi obstacle — one registerTool with optional params is trivially expressible in TypeBox.

verdicts.name: Deterministic .sema write gate (workflow/tool linting hook)
verdicts.notes: Blocking hook is fully supported: pi.on("tool_call") returning {block: true, reason} confirmed (ToolCallEventResult, types.d.ts:747-751; blocked reason is fed back to the model), isToolCallEventType narrowing confirmed (types.d.ts:730-740), tool_result patching for advisory warnings confirmed (ToolResultEventResult, types.d.ts:759-763). `sema workflow check --strict --json` confirmed (Commands at main.rs:616-622, dispatch at 1208-1217 → sema_stdlib::workflow_check; cited 548-624 is drift but the command is real, static, no-LLM). REQUIRED CHANGE: the proposal says 'blocks the write with proposed content' for write AND edit — but EditToolInput is oldText/newText (edit.d.ts), not final file content; for edit events the hook must read the current file and apply the replacement itself to produce the content it lints (or gate only `write` and lint edits post-hoc via tool_result). Write events do carry full content, so the write path works as described.

verdicts.name: Sema subagents: defagent as budgeted, journaled delegation
verdicts.notes: All load-bearing sema primitives confirmed: defagent is a special form (special_forms.rs:57, `__vm-defagent` native per comment at :92) with Agent struct at value.rs:435; the sticky over_budget latch checked at agent entry and by workflow/run after the body is confirmed verbatim (context.rs ~70-77, including the rationale that fan-out swallows leaf Err); :on-tool-call callback exists as an agent/run option (sema-llm builtins.rs:2107) and drives agent.tool_call journal events (workflow_tools_test.rs); --resume with memoization + events.resume-N segments confirmed (journal.rs, main.rs Run{resume}); parallel fan-out engine exists (__fanout-tagged referenced in context.rs). Pi side is just registerTool + pi.exec — trivially supported. Risks are accurately stated: kill-via-signal orphans the run but the journal contract guarantees a valid prefix (journal.rs write() flushes per line). The wrapper-workflow generation is string templating — no API dependency. Only unverified micro-cite: prelude.rs:465-470 for the shim location (mechanism confirmed via tests regardless).

verdicts.name: Skill + prompt export via resources_discover
verdicts.notes: resources_discover confirmed: fires after session_start with reason "startup"|"reload" and handlers return {skillPaths, promptPaths, themePaths} (types.d.ts:392-403, handler registration at 818). pi-sema's stub is indeed empty today (src/hooks/resources.ts:8-12 returns empty arrays). The reload_runtime pattern exists exactly as described: examples/extensions/reload-runtime.ts registers /reload-runtime command + a reload_runtime tool that queues the command via pi.sendUserMessage("/reload-runtime", {deliverAs:"followUp"}) — necessary because ctx.reload() lives only on ExtensionCommandContext (types.d.ts:282), so a tool can't call it directly; the queued-command indirection is the sanctioned path and the proposal already uses it. $ARGUMENTS substitution in prompt templates confirmed (docs/prompt-templates.md:70: `$@` or `$ARGUMENTS`). The reload-teardown risk is real and correctly mitigated — session_shutdown fires with reason "reload" (types.d.ts:447-452) for cleanly killing/respawning the mcp child.

verdicts.name: Hygiene: pi.exec migration + streaming tool renderers
verdicts.notes: Exactly as claimed. pi.exec(command, args, options) at types.d.ts:887; ExecOptions {signal, timeout, cwd} and ExecResult {stdout, stderr, code, killed} confirmed in dist/core/exec.d.ts — killed distinguishes timeout/abort from failure. execute()'s onUpdate callback (types.d.ts:361) + renderResult with isPartial (types.d.ts:299-304) supports streaming. promptSnippet/promptGuidelines confirmed on ToolDefinition (types.d.ts:342-345) and feed the system prompt (agent-session.js _toolPromptSnippets/_toolPromptGuidelines maps); dynamic-tools.ts example exists. Current src/sema.ts is indeed execSync + hand-rolled quoteArg + string-concatenated commands (src/sema.ts:1,37,62) — the migration target is real. The sema eval --json envelope to surface is confirmed (main.rs:1646-1670).

verdicts.name: Upstream: listChanged push notifications (completes the loop with zero polling)
verdicts.notes: Both ends verified. Sema: server.rs:169 currently hardcodes listChanged:false inside the initialize result (cited 165-176 — exact); handle_request is a pure request→Option<Response> function and the async request loop owns the stdout writer, so emitting an unsolicited {"method":"notifications/tools/list_changed"} line after a tools/call that bound new ToolDefs is a genuinely small, structurally easy change (the tool list is already recomputed live from iter_bindings, tools.rs:726). Pi: the bridge is the extension's own stdio reader, so dispatching the notification → re-list → diff → registerTool (auto-activates, verified) / setActiveTools (types.d.ts:893) for removals all works. The interim fallback (re-list after self-initiated eval/run_file calls) needs no upstream change and covers the self-extension loop, as stated. One nuance: 'removed' tools can only be deactivated, never unregistered — and because _refreshToolRegistry only auto-activates names absent from the previous registry, a deactivated-then-re-added same-name tool will NOT re-auto-activate; the bridge must explicitly setActiveTools to re-enable it.

verdicts.name: Sema MCP Bridge (kill the slash commands)
verdicts.notes: All sema-side claims confirmed. handle_request at crates/sema-mcp/src/server.rs:148 implements exactly initialize/ping/tools/list/tools/call over line-delimited JSON-RPC, protocol 2024-11-05, listChanged:false (~server.rs:165-172; notifications correctly get no reply, server.rs:157-160). --include/--exclude confirmed as comma-separated CLI flags (main.rs:328-333) filtered via is_tool_allowed (tools.rs:761-777). Sandbox::allow_all() hardcoded for mcp at main.rs:921 — the unsandboxed-eval risk is real. Tool count checks out: 9 default (run_file/compile/eval/docs/fmt/disasm/build/info/docs_search) + 8 notebook/* = 17 (tools.rs:558-712). Minor: if the bridge passes --include, tools forged later via eval will be filtered out of tools/list — use --exclude-only curation.

verdicts.name: /forge — Create-a-Tool flow (Claude Code /agents, but for deftools)
verdicts.notes: Mechanism sound but the envelope assertion is written against the wrong shape: sema eval --json emits {ok, value, stdout, stderr, error:{message,hint,line,col}, elapsedMs} (main.rs:1860-1894, verified empirically) — NOT flat error_msg/error_hint/error_line/error_col; step (2)'s key checks must read the nested error object. Everything else verified: --timeout is parsed-and-ignored (main.rs:977 `timeout: _timeout`; empirically (sleep 200) with --timeout 50 completed), so pi.exec's timeout is indeed load-bearing; strict sandbox denies shell/fs-write/network/env-write/process/llm/serial, allows fs-read/env-read (sandbox.rs:33-41, verified: (shell "ls") → Permission denied); (tool? x) exists (sema-llm/builtins.rs:4177); SEMA_HOME resolution home.rs:5-13; live injection via mcp eval into the shared global env + per-call tools/list recompute confirmed both structurally (tools.rs:726 iter_bindings, server keeps one Interpreter) and empirically (deftool via mcp eval persisted; tool? → #t on a later call). The strict-sandbox-can't-smoke-LLM-tools risk is accurate (LLM is a denied cap in STRICT).

verdicts.name: Live Workflow Widget (journal-tailing sema_workflow_run tool)
verdicts.notes: Journal contract verified: one JSON line + newline, flushed immediately per event, write errors swallowed so the prefix stays valid JSONL (journal.rs:~125-140). Event vocabulary all present in event.rs: run.started (with phases[] from defworkflow :phases meta, :29-51), phase.started/:56, phase.ended/:61, agent.started/:73, agent.result/:94, agent.tool_call/:108, budget/:144, run.ended/:164, auth.required/:211. run.started.code_version confirmed emitted as empty string (sema-stdlib/src/workflow.rs:241) with metadata.json carrying the real value. SEMA_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID seam at context.rs:33/128. --args/--run-dir flags exist (default .sema/runs, main.rs:559-566). Exit code 2 = needs-auth confirmed (main.rs:~1363 + format_needs_auth_guidance printing sema mcp login lines). events.resume-<n>.jsonl segments confirmed (journal.rs:195-204). Best-effort attribution comment at workflow.rs:536-546 (crate is sema-stdlib/src/workflow.rs, matching the cited lines). Two small additions: (a) on an interactive TTY the run logs in inline instead of exiting 2 — pass --no-auth-prompt for deterministic orchestrator behavior (main.rs:549-590); (b) phases is serde-skipped when empty, so undeclared-:phases workflows have no phases key — checklist rendering must degrade.

verdicts.name: Workflow Runs Overlay Dashboard
verdicts.notes: Sema-side claims all check out. list_runs at workflow_view.rs:300-315 does exactly the described scan: child dirs of run_dir containing events.jsonl, sorted newest-first by the journal's mtime. Default run dir .sema/runs (main.rs:565). result.json/metadata.json sidecars confirmed (journal.rs:147-155); absence-of-run.ended-in-journal as liveness signal is consistent with the frozen event set. events.resume-*.jsonl merge requirement confirmed (journal.rs:54, :195-204). index.db exists as the cross-run SQLite index (sema-workflow/src/lib.rs:29-30, `sema workflow index` backfills it) — skipping it for direct JSONL parsing is valid; prompt/output fields are capped (cap_text in workflow.rs) so line sizes are bounded as claimed. Overlay/TUI specifics are pi-side and out of scope here.

verdicts.name: create_sema_tool — the self-extending loop
verdicts.notes: Core loop verified end-to-end on the sema side, with the same envelope-shape correction as /forge: eval --json errors are nested under error:{message,hint,line,col}, not flat error_msg/error_line (main.rs:1860-1894). Verified: deftool binds via env.set into the global env (special_forms.rs:67-89 register_tool; cited 70-135 range also covers register_agent); the mcp eval tool eval_str_compiled's into the ONE shared Interpreter (tools.rs:965-975); tools/list recomputed from iter_bindings every call (tools.rs:558 + :726) — I reproduced the dyn-add experiment live through the running sema MCP server (deftool via eval persisted across calls, tool? → #t). Sandbox asymmetry risk is real: verification runs under --sandbox strict (denies shell/fs-write/network/llm/etc., sandbox.rs:33-41) but sema mcp is Sandbox::allow_all() (main.rs:921). Two corrections: (1) fix the envelope key assertions; (2) if the bridge launched sema mcp with --include, forged tools won't appear in tools/list (is_tool_allowed, tools.rs:761-777) — curate with --exclude only, or include forged names.

verdicts.name: Tool Library with lazy proxy (progressive disclosure)
verdicts.notes: All claims verified. Filepath mode: sema mcp <files...> evals each file into the server interpreter before serving, exiting 1 on load errors (main.rs:926-940). Privacy: user deftools starting with '_' are skipped, and a :mcp/expose #f (or :private) entry in the params map hides a tool (tools.rs:730-741; the schema builder also strips mcp/* meta keys, tools.rs:32, :415). json_args_to_sema does named→positional mapping with required-param errors, per-type coercion, and rest-param spreading (tools.rs:~310-345 doc + impl). Package path exists: PkgCommands::Init/Publish (main.rs:489-512 → pkg::cmd_init/cmd_publish) with DEFAULT_REGISTRY https://pkg.sema-lang.com (pkg.rs:7). The restart-loaded-only caveat is accurate — filepath evaluation happens once at server start.

verdicts.name: Deterministic .sema write gate (workflow/tool linting hook)
verdicts.notes: Verified: `sema workflow check <file> --strict --json` exists exactly as described (WorkflowCommands::Check, main.rs:614-628), documented as static validation 'WITHOUT evaluating it or calling any LLM'. Both cited diagnostic codes exist: E-WF-SHAPE (sema-stdlib/src/workflow_check.rs:193) and W-STEP-AGENT-TOOLS (:476), plus the full E-*/W-* family (E-PARSE, E-WF-NAME, E-MCP-SPEC, W-PHASE-UNDECL, W-STEP-TOOLS, ...). Note the checker lives in sema-stdlib/src/workflow_check.rs; crates/sema/src/workflow_check.rs is a 6-line re-export shim — the cited main.rs:548-624 range is the CLI enum, correct. The stated limitation is accurate: check_workflow only fires per (defworkflow ...) form, so plain deftool files get no workflow diagnostics; fallbacks exist — `sema fmt --check` (run_fmt with check flag, main.rs:864) and read-many (sema-stdlib/src/io.rs:1602). E-only blocking with W-passthrough matches the Severity split (Diag::error vs Diag::warn).

verdicts.name: Sema subagents: defagent as budgeted, journaled delegation
verdicts.notes: Sema primitives all verified: defagent is a special form on both engines (sema-vm/src/lower.rs:310, compiler.rs:1505; sema-eval/src/special_forms.rs:57, register_agent building Agent{name,system,tools,max_turns,model}); Agent struct at value.rs:435-441 (cited 435-442 ✓); step's :agent branch routes through (agent/run agent prompt {:on-tool-call shim}) at sema-eval/src/prelude.rs:465-475 (cited as prelude.rs:465-470 but note the crate is sema-eval, not a stdlib prelude); agent/name exists (sema-llm/builtins.rs:4274); :budget {:usd} parsed tolerantly (context.rs:146-152) and the sticky over_budget latch is checked at agent entry + by workflow/run after the body (context.rs:71-76, charge :322-343); --resume exists with memo replay (main.rs:578-582); parallel's default concurrency cap is 8, overridable by the trailing arg (prelude.rs:568, __fanout-tagged :548); WF-1 cancellation deferral confirmed (docs/deferred.md:278). One mechanism gap: the generated one-step wrapper defworkflow is run via `sema workflow run <file>`, which evals just that file — the wrapper must (load ...) or textually include the stored defagent definition, since agents in ~/.sema/pi-tools/agents/ aren't auto-loaded by the workflow runner. Also exit-code-2 TTY caveat applies: pass --no-auth-prompt.

verdicts.name: Skill + prompt export via resources_discover
verdicts.notes: Almost entirely pi-side; the only sema-side claims are trivially true: `sema workflow run <file> --args <json>` is the documented CLI (main.rs:555-566, --args default "{}" bound to *workflow-args*), and tool name/description/schema for SKILL.md generation are available from tools/list (Tool with description + inputSchema, tools.rs). The re-eval-on-reconnect idempotency claim holds: deftool/defagent just env.set() their binding (special_forms.rs:74-89), so re-evaluating library files after a runtime reload is safe. No refuting evidence found.

verdicts.name: Hygiene: pi.exec migration + streaming tool renderers
verdicts.notes: Sema-side surface confirmed: `sema eval --json` emits the structured envelope with ok/value/stdout/stderr/elapsedMs and a nested error object carrying message/hint/line/col (main.rs:1860-1894; verified empirically — error case returned {"error":{"col":1,"line":1,"message":...}}). Same naming correction as elsewhere: surface error.line/error.col/error.hint (nested), not error_line/error_col top-level fields. Since sema eval's own --timeout is a no-op (main.rs:977, empirically confirmed), moving timeout enforcement to pi.exec is not just nice-to-have but required correctness — this proposal is the prerequisite fix.

verdicts.name: Upstream: listChanged push notifications (completes the loop with zero polling)
verdicts.notes: Premise verified: capabilities report {tools:{listChanged:false}} and the server never emits notifications (server.rs:~165-172; notifications from the client get None back, server.rs:157-160), while tools/list is already recomputed from the live env every call (tools.rs:558 + iter_bindings :726) — confirmed empirically (deftool via mcp eval appeared without restart). Version 1.30.0 confirmed (Cargo.toml:50). One correction to 'single-file change in server.rs': handle_request is a pure request→response function with no writer access — emitting an unsolicited notification means threading a before/after tool-name snapshot (or a changed flag) through run_mcp_server_on's read/write loop (server.rs:24-120) and writing an extra line after the response; still small and single-crate, but it's a loop restructure plus a snapshot helper, not a capability-flag flip. The interim workaround (client re-lists after self-initiated eval/run_file) is fully supported by the recompute-per-call behavior.
